steps.title: Start a password manager
steps.why: Begin with email and bank. Move the rest as you log in.

steps.title: Run your password manager’s security report
steps.why: Fix anything flagged breached or reused.

steps.title: Run your browser’s password check
steps.why: Fix what it flags as breached or reused.

steps.title: Give email and bank their own passwords
steps.why: The two accounts that unlock the rest.

steps.title: Add an authenticator or passkey to your main email
steps.why: Email resets everything else.

steps.title: Swap text codes for app prompts or a passkey
steps.why: Text codes can be intercepted.

steps.title: Check recovery phone and email
steps.why: Old numbers are a back door.

steps.title: Repeat sign-in protection on your other email accounts
steps.why: Each one can reset something.

steps.title: Add a hardware security key
steps.why: Sign-in that phishing can’t steal.

steps.title: Set a port-out PIN with your carrier
steps.why: Blocks SIM-swap takeovers.

steps.title: Turn on automatic updates
steps.why: Most attacks use bugs that are already patched.

steps.title: Screen lock with biometrics
steps.why: Your phone holds most of your logins.

steps.title: Remove old apps with access to your account
steps.why: Forgotten grants keep working.

steps.title: Lockdown Mode or Advanced Protection
steps.why: For people likely to be targeted.

steps.title: Check your emails on Have I Been Pwned
steps.why: See what leaked, then fix those accounts.

steps.title: Turn on breach alerts
steps.why: Hear about the next one early.

steps.title: Remove yourself from people-search sites
steps.why: Do it by hand, or pay a service to repeat it.

steps.title: Send GDPR erasure requests to data brokers
steps.why: You have the right. A generator writes the letters.

steps.title: Remove your contact details from Google results
steps.why: Hides phone and address from search.

steps.title: Freeze your credit at all three bureaus
steps.why: Blocks new credit in your name. Free.

steps.title: Turn on transaction alerts
steps.why: Spot fraud within minutes.

steps.title: Ask your bank to switch off voice ID
steps.why: Cloned voices have passed these checks. Use the number on your card.

steps.title: Use app or key sign-in at your bank
steps.why: Avoid text codes where you can.

steps.title: Switch your voicemail greeting to the default
steps.why: A recorded greeting is a free voice sample.

steps.title: List where your voice is public
steps.why: Seconds of audio can be enough to clone it.

steps.title: Limit who sees videos with your voice
steps.why: Fewer samples to clone from.

steps.title: Turn on YouTube likeness detection
steps.why: Flags AI videos using your face. Needs ID and a selfie.

steps.title: Set up likeness monitoring across the web
steps.why: Watches for your face beyond YouTube.

steps.title: Agree a family safe word
steps.why: Ask for it. Never say it first.

steps.title: Agree a callback rule for money requests
steps.why: Hang up. Call back on a number you already have.

steps.title: Brief older relatives
steps.why: They’re the main target of voice scams.

steps.title: Turn off training in ChatGPT
steps.why: Settings → Data controls.

steps.title: Turn off training in Claude
steps.why: Settings → Privacy.

steps.title: Turn off Gemini activity
steps.why: Stops chats being kept for review and training.

steps.title: Turn off training in Microsoft Copilot
steps.why: Profile → Privacy.

steps.title: Check Meta AI training settings
steps.why: Public posts are used for training.

steps.title: Turn off LinkedIn AI training
steps.why: On by default.

steps.title: Turn off GitHub Copilot training
steps.why: Personal accounts were opted in in April 2026.

steps.title: Review what your assistants remember
steps.why: Memory collects personal details over time.

steps.title: List what each agent can reach
steps.why: Email, files, payments.

steps.title: Require a confirm before agents send or pay
steps.why: Web pages can carry hidden instructions.

steps.title: Revoke agent connections you don’t use
steps.why: Idle access is pure risk.

steps.title: Keep agents out of banking sessions
steps.why: A logged-in agent can be steered.

steps.title: Store backup codes offline
steps.why: Your way back in if the phone is lost.

steps.title: Bookmark where to report fraud
steps.why: Fast reports help recovery.

steps.title: Know the deepfake takedown routes
steps.why: For intimate images, real or fake.

questions.label: Passwords
questions.text: How do you keep track of your passwords?

options.label: My browser or phone saves them
options.note: That counts as a password manager.

options.label: A few I reuse
options.note: Most common. Start with email and bank, not everything at once.

options.label: Written down at home
options.note: Safer than reuse. A manager adds breach checks.

questions.label: Security report
questions.text: When did you last open its security report?

options.label: Didn’t know it had one
options.note: Most do. It lists breached and reused passwords.

questions.label: Email accounts
questions.text: Which email accounts do you use?

questions.label: Main email
questions.text: Which one gets your password-reset emails?

questions.label: Email sign-in
questions.text: How do you sign in to {mainEmail}?

options.label: Just a password
options.note: The single biggest gap. Ten minutes.

options.label: Password, then a text message code
options.note: Better. An app prompt is stronger.

options.label: Password, then an app or phone prompt

questions.label: Updates
questions.text: When your phone offers an update, you…

options.label: Never see it, it installs itself
US
options.note: A credit freeze is the biggest lever.

questions.label: Bank voice ID
questions.text: Has your bank ever recognised you by voice?
questions.hint: “My voice is my password” or similar.

options.label: Yes, I use voice ID
options.note: Cloned voices have passed these checks. One call turns it off.

questions.label: Panicked call
questions.text: Someone close calls in a panic, in their voice, asking for money now. What happens?

options.label: I ask for our safe word
I hang up and call them back
options.note: Good instinct. A safe word makes it automatic.

options.label: Honestly, I’d probably help
options.note: Most people would. Ten minutes fixes it.

questions.label: Voice & face online
questions.text: How much of your voice and face is online?

options.label: Videos or podcasts with my voice
Barely anything
options.note: Your voicemail greeting may still be your voice.

questions.label: AI assistants
questions.text: Which AI assistants do you use?

questions.label: AI acting for you
questions.text: Do any of them act for you?

options.label: They read my email or files
They browse, book or buy
options.note: The newest risk. Two settings matter most.
